title: 20-Year Treasury Bond auction (December first reopening) — the first long-duration Treasury coupon ever auctioned this late in December
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 for this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), text layer inflated stream-by-stream and re-tokenised — an independent third read of the primary both proposing sweeps used. Row reads verbatim `20-Year  BOND` + `R` (Treasury's reopening marker) / announcement `Thursday, December 17, 2026` / auction `Wednesday, December 23, 2026` / settlement `Monday, December 28, 2026`. The same fetch shows `20-Year  BOND` WITHOUT the `R` on 2026-11-18 and `20-Year  BONDR` again on 2027-01-20, which is what fixes this sale as the FIRST reopening of the November CUSIP rather than the second. The 1:00 p.m. ET bidding deadline is NOT from the schedule — it is fiscaldata `auctions_query`'s `closing_time_comp`, which reads `01:00 PM` on all 77 20-Year auctions since the tenor's 2020-05 revival (same-day pull, HTTP 200, 275,209 bytes). Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 2026-12-17 announcement itself, which has not happened
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read both prior proposals in full first per EVENT-RESEARCH.md: `.from-treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20.json` (the successor sale, which proposed this as its own direct predecessor) and `.from-treasury-2y-frn-2026-12-23.json` (the same-day FRN, whose 11:30 a.m. closing-time call depends on this security taking the 1:00 p.m. coupon slot). Both are now shadowed and inert. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH CHANGED ABOUT THEIR FRAMING. Both proposals called this 'the latest December 20-Year on record' — true, and an UNDERSTATEMENT. Measured this session across the full nominal-coupon census (fiscaldata `auctions_query`, security_type Note+Bond, 2010-01-11 onward, 1,281 nominal auctions after excluding TIPS and FRNs, two paged fetches, HTTP 200): NO long-duration coupon — 10-Year, 20-Year or 30-Year — has EVER auctioned on or after December 22 in the entire sample. The latest long-end December auction on record is December 21. 2026-12-23 is not a late instance of a known slot; it is the first observation of a slot that has never existed. THE COUNTERPART CORRECTION, ALSO MEASURED: the 'thinnest dealer-balance-sheet week of the year' framing is wrong about the week. 37 of 103 December coupon auctions (36%) sold on or after the 23rd, and Treasury has run a 2-Year/5-Year/7-Year block in that terminal week for 16 consecutive years without a break — the calendar already tracks this cycle's as treasury-2y-note-2026-12-28, treasury-5y-note-2026-12-28 and treasury-7y-note-2026-12-29. The week is Treasury's most reliably-used December week; what is unprecedented is putting DURATION in it. SIZE: $13B expected on a 24-of-24 reopening base rate, published in the 2026-11-04 refunding statement and read back at the 2026-12-17 announcement — owned by the coupon-announcement lane, deliberately not re-registered here. GRADING SLOT: this is a leg-1 (FIRST) reopening, so the applicable yardstick is the constant-$13B first-reopening band (n=12: floor 2.50 · p25 2.64 · median 2.74 · p75 2.75 · ceiling 2.79), NOT the second-reopening band treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20 derived and NOT the new-issue grid treasury-20y-bond-2026-11-18 warns about. Proposed and kept as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
